div.head: Af 7
div.ab: VIII. Gif hwa in cyninges healle gefeohte oððe his wæpn gebrede, ⁊ hine mon gefó, sie ðæt on cyninges dome, swa deað swa lif, swa he him forgifan wille.
VIII. Gif hwa on kyninges healle gefeohte oþþe wæpen gebrede, ⁊ hine mon gefó, sy ðæt on cyninges dóme, swa deað swa lif, swa he him forgyfan wille.
Be ðam þæt man feohteð on kyninges healle. Gyf hwá on kyninges halle gefeohte oððe his wæpne gebrede, ⁊ hine mon gefó, sy þæt on cyninges dome, swa deað swa lif, swa he him forgyfan wylle.
Si quis in domo regis pugnet uel arma extrahat et capiatur, sit in arbitrio regis sic uita sic mors, sicut ei condonare uoluerit.
[Be ðam þæt man feohteð on kyninges healle.] Gif hwa in cyninges healle gefeohte, oððe his wæpn gebrede, ⁊ hine mon gefó, sie ðæt on cyninges dome, swa deað swa lif, swa he him forgifan wille.
{VIII} Gif hwa in cyninges healle gefeohte, oððe his wæpn gebrede, ⁊ hine mon gefó, sie ðæt on cyninges dome, swa deað swa lif, swa he him forgifan wille.
Wenn jemand in der Königshalle ficht oder seine Waffe zückt, und man ihn [dabei] verhaftet, stehe es in des Königs Entscheidung, so Tod wie Leben, falls dieser ihm vergeben will.
If someone fights in the king’s hall or draws his weapon, and he is arrested [in the act], let it be at the king’s decision, death or life, if he is willing to pardon him.

If anyone fights or draws his weapon in the king's hall, and [if he] is arrested, it shall be for the king to decide whether he shall be put to death, or permitted to live, in case the king is willing to forgive him.
If anyone fights or draws his weapon in the king’s hall, and he is captured, it is to be at the king’s judgment, whether he will grant him death or life.
If someone fights in the king’s hall or draws his weapon, and he is caught, let it be according to the king’s judgment: either death or life, whichever the king wishes to grant him.

note.quote: four of five Alfredian uses of 'gefeohtan' are scattered ramifications of Ine's law on fighting before the privileged (n. 34)

note.label: much the same as
note.quote: Alfred's law on fights in a king's hall was much the same as Ine's, but for Alfred the offence included drawing a weapon

note.label: compare
note.quote: Compare to Ine §6, which requires in addition that the aggressor lose all that he owns.

Der Satz benutzt wohl, ändert aber Ine 6. Er erweitert den Fall durch Waffenzücken (s. d. Gl 4) und qualifiziert ihn durch Handhaftigkeit; er nennt den Königshof (s. Gl 2) prächtiger ‘Halle’. Den Satz benutzt II Cn 59. Vgl. Gl Blutig fechten 5a—e; Begnadigung 6. — In letzter Zeile verstehe ich swa (s. Wb III D) als ‘wenn’; dagegen Wülfing, Toller ‘wie dieser ihm zuerkennen will’; diese Bed. ohne hinzugedachtes Objekt scheint nicht nachgewiesen und ‘ihm Tod forgiefan’ (s. d. Wb 3) wohl nicht Agsächsisch

The sentence probably draws on Ine 6, but alters it. It extends the case to the drawing of a weapon (see that word in Gl 4) and qualifies it by the offender’s being caught in the act; it calls the king’s court (see Gl 2) more grandly ‘hall’. The sentence is used by II Cn 59. Cf. Gl Blutig fechten 5a—e; Begnadigung 6. — In the last line I take swa (see Wb III D) as ‘if’; Wülfing and Toller, on the other hand, have ‘as he will adjudge to him’; this meaning without an understood object seems not to be attested, and ‘forgiefan death to him’ (see that word in Wb 3) is probably not Anglo-Saxon
So also Liebermann. Possibly, however, the words may mean ‘on such terms as the king is willing (to forgive him).’
